sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content: each entry gives the village, neighbouring languages as reported by residents (Podena, Biriduwa, Orya, Kapitaw, Maremgi) and dialectometry percentages (Mawes Wares 81-100 percent different from Mawes Dey, Mander, Podena; Mawes Dey 91-99.75 percent different from its neighbours). The underlying Badan Bahasa field wordlists are not published on the site.

sources.citation: Widiatmika, Putu Wahyu & Dendi Wijaya. 2025. Tracing Languages in the Philippines and Indonesia. Presentation slides (26 pp.), LAWAS series, National Commission for Culture and the Arts (Philippines); posted September 2025. LexStat cognate-detection heatmap and phylogenetic tree over Philippine and Indonesian wordlists including 'Mawes Wares and Mawesdai (isolate)'.
sources.note: No phonology content. The slides present LexStat cognate similarity ('Mawesdai and Mawes Wares similarities'; 'Distant languages: Mawes and Abui'), a tree listing 'Mawes Wares and Mawesdai (isolate)', and a table of the word for 'one' (Mawes Wares mendakai, Mawesdai mendakai); no transcription conventions, no stress or tone marks, no statement about the sound system.

sources.citation: Hammarström, Harald. 2010. The status of the least documented language families in the world. Language Documentation & Conservation 4: 177-212 (Mawes: section 2.4.12, p. 189).
sources.note: Nothing. Mawes is treated only for classification and documentation status: total published data = 'ca 250 words and 15 sentences'; notes that 250 words + 15 sentences 'will appear in an SIL Indonesia survey report (Wambaliau 2006)'. No phonological remark of any kind.

Anceaux collection of wordlists of Irian Jaya languages B: Non-Austronesian (Papuan) languages, Part I (Irian Jaya Source Materials 9, Series B 3). Leipzig: MPI-EVA (asjp.clld.org).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Nothing: 107 forms for the ASJP 40(100)-item list in ASJPcode (e.g. kidam I, nam thou, inem/mia we, mendakai one, yakeneu two, defar head, nonsom eye, deNkin tree), loan flags all False; ASJPcode carries no stress or tone marks and the page has no phonological notes, so whatever accent marking Anceaux's originals may have had is not recoverable here.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Central and Western Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study, vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene, 345-460. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Canberra: Research School of Pacific Studies, ANU. Mawes: sections 2.6.2.2.11.1.0, 2.6.2.2.11.1.6 and 2.6.2.2.11.1.8, pp. 411-414.
sources.note: No phonology content for Mawes (or for any Tor-Lake Plain language). The chapter gives classification, location, speaker numbers and a pronoun chart (Mawes: kidam 'I', inem 'we', nam 'you sg.', nem 'you pl.', enem(?) 'he') and states: 'Very little is known about the languages of the stock; the only data available are wordlists of at most 150 items, and only few of these have been published.. the writer relied on unpublished lists from Anceaux' collection (Tor River languages, Mawes, Uria, Taworta-Aero)'. The general TNG phonology remarks elsewhere in the chapter are not about Mawes.
sources.venue: New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Pacific Linguistics B-31. Canberra: ANU. Entry no. 90 'Mawes Family-Level Isolate' (p. 41); wordlist column '90. MAWES (Ac)' (p. 110).
sources.note: Nothing. Entry lists villages Mawes Wares, Mawes Dai and sources 'Galis 1955 (N, Wl; S); U4' (unpublished Anceaux). The 39-item wordlist is given in a deliberately unified comparative orthography 'which is neither phonemic nor accurately phonemic' (Note on the orthography, wordlist appendix); no stress marks anywhere.

sources.citation: Robide van der Aa, P. J. B. C. (ed.). 1879. Reizen naar Nederlandsch Nieuw-Guinea ondernomen op last der Regeering van Nederlandsch-Indie in de jaren 1871, 1872, 1875-1876 door de Heeren P. van der Crab en J. E. Teysmann, J. G. Coorengel en A. J. Langeveldt van Hemert en P. Swaan, met geschied- en aardrijkskundige toelichtingen. 's-Gravenhage: Martinus Nijhoff (KITLV). Van der Crab's 1871 voyage: kampong Mawes, Walckenaersbaai (pp. 112-113) and general remarks on Papuan languages (pp. 127-128).
sources.note: Nothing about Mawes phonology. On Mawes: 'Hunne taal was ook den tolk geheel onverstaanbaar en geleek weinig, naar hetgeen op de naburige plaatsen gehoord was.' The generic sentence 'In de meeste Papoesche woorden en vooral in de plaatsnamen valt de klemtoon op de laatste lettergreep' (p. 127) is a traveller's impression across all of north/west New Guinea and must not be attributed to Mawes; the compilers footnote there concerns Numfor (Mefoorsch) stress after van Hasselt's grammar.

sources.citation: Saad, George & I Komang Sumaryana Putra. Documentation of Mawes: An endangered language isolate from northwest New Guinea. ELAR deposit mawes-saad-0828 (ELDP grant IPF1036), status 'Forthcoming'.
sources.note: Deposit page only: Mawes described as an isolate with 500-750 speakers on the north coast of Sarmi Regency; 'first major documentation' of the language; no materials yet available, no phonology notes.
